html:
The Crow, who call themselves Apsáalooke, are a Siouan-speaking people of the Yellowstone River country in present Montana and Wyoming. They split from the farming Hidatsa of the Missouri River, now part of the Three Affiliated Tribes, probably in the 1600s or earlier, and with horses became mounted bison hunters.

Hemmed in by stronger enemies, the Lakota and the Blackfoot, they often sided with the United States. Crow scouts rode with Custer before the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876, fought on land that is now within their reservation. Their chief Plenty Coups led them through the early reservation years. The Crow Reservation in southern Montana is one of the largest in the country, and its yearly Crow Fair is a major gathering. Earlier maps show them as Crow.
